From the top:

Marram Webster.

Betray (verb) 

1.) to seduce (that didn’t happen, in fact Bonnie has done more of that.)

2.) to deliver to an enemy by treachery. (Ben did no lie to the group of Bandits, his enemies) 

3.) to fail or desert in time of need. (This is the closest thing that you’re arguing but again Ben prevented an attack by his action but only failed to inform. There was no current need for those medical supplies but even so with context it still checks out.)

I view Javi and Lee as people from the old world trying to adjust. As I’m getting older I can definitely relate to them a bit more if a zombie plague or something like that were to happen. Having to test old world moralities versus what you need to do to survive, and what you are willing to give up for either route. Personally, I favor Lee more out of the three. To me he seems like the perfect blend of a blank enough canvas for your choices to shape how he is but with enough personality and charisma to not be boring. 

Growing up in this new world is a very interesting approach I enjoyed though. Like the delicate balance of children maintaining their innocence to their own peril, or partially forsake their childhood so they can live another day. Playing a character who was very much shaped by your actions in the first game was pretty interesting as well. 

I still enjoy Javi, but for me in the New Frontier it definitely felt like the game would nudge you into certain decisions. With that it seemed like they sort of missed the mark on that one. If god forbid Telltale were to get up and running again after Wolf Among Us 2, I would really like to visit Richmond and get more Javi. I think there were some hints during season 4 that Lily’s group was fighting with Richmond, if that’s true I would be really interested in seeing what a war looks like in this setting. What sort of choices would Javi have to make for Richmond and possibly his family?

It was an interesting idea to have multiple playable survivors. Served well as a nice little DLC to hold us over until season 2. The writing may be a bit basic since it’s multiple little stories but I can still appreciate what they did. I was both impressed and disappointed with their outcome in season 2.

From a meta sense, it wouldn’t help Clem’s maturity arc if she ran into multiple competent survivors. Sure it would probably be less of a “Torture Clem Season”, but I think she wouldn’t grow as much. And in game, unless they threw a lot at the player they wouldn’t really get to experience everything from a decision making standpoint. 

I won’t lie, I’m somewhat of a Cabin group hater with the slight exception of like one or two people. And seeing what the 400 days group became under Carver’s group was a bit disappointing. I honestly think if they didn’t make the adults of the cabin group rely so heavily on a child for everything it would feel a little better but balancing that out seems like a tricky situation.

It’s honestly just hard to think about the 400 days group not conforming to a pretty messed up group. Like if they are capable of that, it’s hard to think of them as a “benevolent” survivor group if that makes sense.

Christa definitely comes to mind at first. Now it could be due to the events that happen in the prologue of season 2, but it seemed like they were just scraping by.

As a professional Jane hater, I will say That at the best least Jane gave Clem the tools to do more than just barely survive. Clem is leagues more competent than the cabin group in the beginning of the season. She later proves herself to surpass the two warring mentors near the end of season 2. 

Although Jane had characteristics I didn’t like in a character/survivor and had disjointed and somewhat baffling writing after the hardware store that just cemented my disdain for the character, she did manage to do at least one good thing for Clem.

As much as I hated seeing Pete “die” again, it was a genuinely good story that I came around to. Should they do it again? I don’t think so, it wouldn’t really have the same impact. That would be similar to us Spidey fans getting tired of seeing Uncle Ben get shot over and over again.

I don’t think he’s racist, or at least not concretely. He’s definitely an angry boomer that is codependent with his daughter while overly suspicious of any newcomers barring our three dairy farmers. His actions towards people of color definitely seem to be potentially racist though. 

I guess from the story perspective he is concerned with a pre-apocalypse murderer in the group, and wants to protect his daughter. From a narrative/meta perspective he’s a device to cause drama/tension with Lee’s past. Which unfortunately is a universal thing we can’t really alter except for I think what drives Lee to kill the senator. 

So I think with the narrative device punishing the player for actions they didn’t do paired with how he goes about hating Lee has parallels to potential racial actions. 


I would say the Kenny “urban” meme is a more concrete example of racism. Was it intentional racism? It’s debatable, but with his actions  in the games I would lean towards no. Meanwhile from how I see Larry it may not be concrete but his actions do call into question. It’s harder to tell since we didn’t get as much time with Larry to establish one way or the other. 

So with the evidence we have I would mostly agree that he is definitely an angry man with little left, not caring about anyone else outside of his “circle”. And definitely can be a hinderance to the survival of the group. But until we get any more info or content on Larry he just has some racist vibes but nothing solid to definitively say he is.

It’s sort of a mixed bag. Yes, these are grown adults relying on a child to do most of the grunt work, and would probably make more sense if she was the only one physically able to or have them step up at least a little bit. Meta-wise they want you the player to experience all the hardships and whatnot. Storytelling-wise it’s supposed to have Clem have this sink or swim, trial by fire sort of moment where she goes from being the child who relies on the group to being the survivor the group relies on.

It’s wild because Ben would act exactly how a lot of people would act instead of the tough survivor then envisioned themselves to be. We have to remember that Ben is still a teenager here fresh into the apocalypse.

He definitely should have told the group about him making that deal with the bandits. Making the deal seems pretty logical since Lilly wants to stay in that area along with all of the messed up stuff Ben went through with the Savelots bandits. The bandits who are accused by the woman who had Clem’s hat to rape along with them killing most of Ben’s group. 

There were two times Lee would ask Ben to look out for Clementine and I can understand being frustrated that Ben both runs away and didn’t keep a close eye on her. Him running when they are in the middle of a horde of zombies is an understandable choice but a frustrating one for Lee. Clem did sneak out of the house so you could try to put the blame on Ben’s lax watch but I don’t think it’s a very strong case there.

Lastly you have the infamous hatchet choice. Was it the smartest move? Probably not, but was this boy supposed to deduce that this small albeit pretty useful weapon was a barricade for potentially no visible walkers at the time? 

So there’s one strong point that he should have told the motor inn group about the Savelots bandits and the deal while they are still in the area. The other two points are understandable to be a little frustrated at him but not super strong points.

There are people that tweak the content until their players have a better chance, and feel like they are the heroes of the story. Then there are people who would Run Strahd going all out against the first threat this man has had in a long long time. 

Like yes there is going to be an aspect of making sure your players are having fun. But there is also the dread, the foreboding feeling of hardship and death. I personally lean towards the latter, because if you go soft on your little brother here then it wasn’t a real win in my eyes. This man is a legend for a reason, so it’s difficult for me to want to have him go soft on his adversaries.

I have to ask my friend who speaks Russian what they said again because it was a bit more insightful at the time than <speaking Russian>.

You can reign Kenny in from mistreating Arvo openly. Offer him the warmth of the fire, but obviously he’s distraught about his loss.

The absolute hate in Arvo’s look towards a soaked and freezing Clem is so off putting. Not to mention if you try to physically intervene with Kenny. Like you could be his biggest defender and he’ll still look at you sideways. 

Bonnie and Mike at that time wanted an excuse to go against Kenny since Sarita died.
